title: Wake up America! Civilization calls every man, woman and child!
description: WWI recruitment poster by James Montgomery Flagg (1917) depicting Columbia — the female personification of America — sleeping, dressed in patriotic stars and stripes and wearing a Phrygian cap. The figure of Columbia, modeled on actress Mary Arthur, embodies the nation's allegorical identity. One of the most iconic American female allegorical images of the First World War, later reproduced as one of the most widely distributed WWI posters. Published for 'Wake Up, America' Day, April 19, 1917.

title: Columbia calls—Enlist now for U.S. Army
description: WWI recruitment poster (1917) depicting Columbia standing on the globe atop North America, holding the American flag and a sword, calling men to enlist. Designed by Frances Adams Halsted (who also wrote the accompanying poem) and painted by Vincente Aderente. After the U.S. entered WWI on April 6, 1917, Halsted donated the design to the War Department; the New York Times planned 500,000 copies. A canonical example of Columbia as female national allegory in wartime American visual culture.

title: Ex-libris da Biblioteca Nacional (A Mulher-Biblioteca)
description: Ex-libris criado por Eliseu Visconti em 1903 para a Biblioteca Nacional do Rio de Janeiro, ainda em uso atualmente. A composição central mostra 'A Mulher-Biblioteca' de perfil: figura feminina de cabelos fartos presos em coque de íris (símbolo entre deuses e homens), folheando um livro aberto sobre balcão, com globo terrestre ao centro. A alegoria feminina da Biblioteca relaciona-se diretamente com a tradição iconográfica das virtudes e das musas.
citation_abnt: VISCONTI, Eliseu. Ex-libris da Biblioteca Nacional. 1903. Desenho, tinta. Biblioteca Nacional, Rio de Janeiro. Projeto Eliseu Visconti, A803. Disponível em: https://eliseuvisconti.com.br/obra/a803/. Acesso em: 19 maio 2026.
notes: AI first-pass (iconocode-sonnet5), imagem unica digitalizada via eliseuvisconti.com.br (alta resolucao), sem inspecao fisica. Ex-libris Art Nouveau: mulher em perfil lendo/escrevendo junto a globo terrestre e estantes, com a inscricao 'BIBLIOTHECA NACIONAL DO RIO DE JANEIRO' -- funciona como dispositivo estatal de marca de posse (inscricao_estatal=3) e e desenhado para reproducao em massa (carimbo em cada livro da colecao; serialidade=3, confirmado por 3 variantes de prova em verde visiveis na mesma folha). description: Allegorical painting of Justice in the Mayor's Cabinet of Brussels City Hall, by Joseph Stallaert. A Belgian civic example connecting female virtue to political authority.

title: Palais de Justice de Bruxelles (Joseph Poelaert)
description: The Brussels Palace of Justice — one of the largest courthouses ever built and a monument to 19th-century legal grandeur. The 'pompous staircase with sculptures attired in Roman robes' and allegorical female figures throughout. Poelaert's design made the Belgian state visible through classical feminine allegory. Central to the dissertation's Belgian case study and Huygebaert's colonial paternalism analysis.

title: Monument aux Pionniers Belges au Congo — La Race Noire Accueillie par la Belgique
description: La Belgique seated, holding torch, lifting veil for a semi-nude African woman presenting her children. description: Painting showing the personification of Justice as a half-length nude female figure against dark background, holding sword and scales. Inscribed 'GERECHTIGKAEIT'. title: Germania
description: Personificação da Alemanha como mulher guerreira (Germania), pintada por Friedrich August von Kaulbach em agosto de 1914, no início da Primeira Guerra Mundial. A figura feminina erguida aparece com coroa imperial de estilo otoniano, espada desembainhada, escudo heráldico e couraça feminina, em fundo noturno com horizonte em chamas. Kaulbach representa a Alemanha em postura defensiva e bélica, simbolizando a nação armada e pronta para o combate. A obra foi encomendada como resposta visual ao clima de mobilização nacional alemã de agosto de 1914, funcionando como propaganda patriótica de alto refinamento artístico.
citation_abnt: KAULBACH, Friedrich August von. Germania. 1914. 1 pintura (óleo sobre tela). Berlim: Deutsches Historisches Museum. Disponível em: https://www.dhm.de/lemo/bestand/objekt/gemaelde-friedrich-august-von-kaulbach-germania-1914. Acesso em: 28 mar. 2026.

title: [Alegoría de la República española y la República francesa]
description: Allegorical drawing or print depicting the Spanish Republic and the French Republic as paired female figures. Produced in the context of the proclamation of the Second Spanish Republic (April 14, 1931), evoking the fraternal bond between the two republican nations. Part of the BNE's collection of drawings, engravings, and photographs relating to the Second Republic. The Spanish Republic figure wears the Phrygian cap and holds attributes of justice and liberty, mirroring the Marianne iconotype of France.
citation_abnt: ALEGORÍA de la República española y la República francesa. 1931. 1 desenho/gravura. Biblioteca Nacional de España, Madrid. Disponível em: https://bdh.bne.es/bnesearch/detalle/76944.

title: Alegoría de la Primera República española (La Flaca)
description: Ilustração satírica publicada na revista republicana La Flaca (Barcelona, 1869–1873), em período correspondente à Primeira República espanhola (fev. 1873 – dez. 1874). Tomás Padró i Pedret, ilustrador principal da publicação, representou a República española como figura feminina, frequentemente com barrete frígio, acompanhada de líderes políticos como Castelar, Pi y Margall, Figueras e Salmerón. La Flaca foi o principal veículo de iconografia republicana federal durante o Sexênio Democrático, e suas alegorias femininas da Espanha constituem corpus fundamental para a história da iconografia política espanhola oitocentista.
citation_abnt: PADRÓ I PEDRET, Tomás. Alegoría de la Primera República española. La Flaca, Barcelona, 1873. 1 litografia. Madri: Biblioteca Nacional de España, Hemeroteca Digital. Disponível em: https://hemerotecadigital.bne.es/hd/es/card?sid=3971781. Acesso em: 28 mar. 2026.

title: 5 Pesetas "Hispania Reclinada" — Gobierno Provisional
description: Hispania reclinada coroada com coroa mural, apoiada nos Pireneus com Gibraltar a seus pés, segurando ramo de oliveira. Mar e raios de sol ao fundo. Moeda fundacional da Espanha pós-monárquica, cunhada apenas durante o breve Gobierno Provisional.
citation_abnt: 5 Pesetas "Hispania Reclinada" — Gobierno Provisional

title: 1 Peseta "Hispania Sentada" — II República
description: Hispania sentada sobre plinto, segurando ramo de oliveira. Última peseta de prata jamais cunhada. A continuidade da pose sentada de 1870 a 1933 revela a *Nachleben* da mesma *Pathosformel* através de duas rupturas fundacionais distintas.
citation_abnt: 1 Peseta "Hispania Sentada" — II República

title: Thronende Justitia / Allegorie der strafenden Gerechtigkeit
description: Photograph of a ceiling fresco in Koblenz showing Justitia enthroned — the allegorical female figure of criminal justice. A German example of Justice as a seated female sovereign figure, wielding punitive authority from a throne-like position.
citation_abnt: ZICK, Januarius. Thronende Justitia / Allegorie der strafenden Gerechtigkeit. [séc. XVIII]. Fotografia de Schulze-Marburg, Rudolf, 1943-1944. Zentralinstitut für Kunstgeschichte. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/201/item_IBA5QWMUFFBZOLE2SPIJO5QD2SPIZS6S.

title: Time and Justice Reveal the Truth
description: Allegorical depiction showing Time and Justice revealing Truth. Belgian example of the Justice-Truth triad where Justice is personified as a woman who, together with Time, unveils Truth — a visual argument for the transparency of law.
citation_abnt: WALKER, Johan. Time and justice reveal the truth. [s.d.]. Royal Institute for Cultural Heritage. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/2048001/AP_10342206.
notes: Confirmed 0.5. Pre-endurecimento baseline — soft founding visual vocabulary.

title: Justitia (Jacob Matham)
description: Print depicting Justitia — the female allegorical figure of Justice with her traditional attributes (scales, sword). By Jacob Matham, a major Dutch engraver, student of Hendrick Goltzius.
citation_abnt: MATHAM, Jacob. Justitia. c. 1600. 1 gravura. Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/89/item_ZCR4KC47OMJN7DRRDFTIWRQS33M7PBN2.

title: Allegory of Justice (Charles Audran after B.P. Cortona)
description: Allegorical representation of Justice, engraved by Charles Audran after an invention by Pietro da Cortona (Berrettini). Italian Baroque model of Justice as a female figure — one of the visual templates that circulated across Europe and eventually reached the Americas.
citation_abnt: AUDRAN, Charles. Allegory of Justice. [séc. XVII]. 1 gravura. Casanatense Library. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/446/RML0348941.

title: Justitia (Hans Kels d. J.)
description: Golden gilded relief sculpture depicting Justitia. A Renaissance example of the female allegorical figure of justice rendered in precious materials — connecting legal symbolism to material luxury and sovereign authority.
citation_abnt: KELS, Hans d. J. Justitia. [séc. XVI]. 1 relevo dourado. Kunsthistorisches Museum Wien. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/15502/KK_6068.

title: Justitia, Allegory of Justice (Johann Oswald Harms)
description: Drawing depicting Justitia — allegorical female figure of justice with scales and sword. German Baroque representation of the legal feminine allegory.
citation_abnt: HARMS, Johann Oswald. Justitia, allegory of justice. [séc. XVII]. 1 desenho. Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/89/item_MH6IXNHWTECBQCNPU7IIMCFP2BDFAV76.

title: Justitia civilis (Maarten de Vos)
description: Allegorical depiction of civil justice (Justitia civilis) by Flemish master Maarten de Vos. Distinction between civil and criminal justice personified as separate female figures — important for understanding the multiplication of legal feminine allegories.
citation_abnt: VOS, Maarten de. Justitia civilis. [séc. XVI]. Royal Institute for Cultural Heritage. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/2048001/AP_10133590.
notes: Confirmed 0.8. Slightly higher than EU-002 (0.5) due to proto-serial print production.

title: Allegory with Justizia, crowned by a putto
description: Allegorical representation of Justizia resting on clouds, being crowned by a putto (cherub), with scales visible. Justice as a celestial female figure receiving divine coronation — the theological dimension of legal allegory.
citation_abnt: WALDMANN, Kaspar. Allegory with Justizia, resting on a cloudbank, crowned by a putto. [séc. XVIII]. 1 desenho. Albertina Museum. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/15508/30435.

title: Female Allegory (Pierre Puvis de Chavannes)
description: Female allegorical figure by Pierre Puvis de Chavannes, the great French muralist whose public commissions (Sorbonne, Panthéon, Hôtel de Ville) defined the visual language of Third Republic civic spaces. This drawing connects to the larger programme of republican allegorical decoration.
citation_abnt: PUVIS DE CHAVANNES, Pierre. Female allegory. [séc. XIX]. 1 desenho. Albertina Museum. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/15508/DG1918_7.

title: La Justice, la Vengeance et la Vérité
description: Engraving depicting three female allegorical figures: Justice, Vengeance, and Truth. A powerful composition showing Justice as a dominant female presence, flanked by Truth and divine Vengeance — key triad in French republican allegorical vocabulary.
citation_abnt: CHIFFLART, François-Nicolas. La Justice, la Vengeance et la Vérité. 1865. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b531737635.
notes: Key counter-example anchoring LOW end of endurecimento. Atlas: Painel I.

title: Le triomphe de la Justice et de la Vérité
description: Engraving showing the triumph of Justice and Truth as female allegorical figures. Complete state with full lettering. Part of Chifflart's series on juridical allegory.
citation_abnt: CHIFFLART, François-Nicolas. Le triomphe de la Justice et de la Vérité. 1865. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b531737529.
notes: Transitional body-to-monument. Zwischenraum visible. Atlas: Painel II.

title: L'envoyé de la Justice
description: Engraving titled 'The Envoy of Justice' — depicting a figure sent by Justice (as a female allegorical power). Early example in the series of Justice representations by Chifflart.
citation_abnt: CHIFFLART, François-Nicolas. L'envoyé de la Justice. 1859. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b53173732g.
notes: EXCEPTIONAL for thesis. Demonstrates DELEGATION mechanism in Contrato Sexual Visual. Atlas: Painel II.

title: Marianne enseignant l'alphabet à des enfants (naïades et Marianne)
description: Engravings depicting naiads and Marianne teaching the alphabet to children. Powerful image of the Republic-as-woman as educator — embodying the republican ideal of laïcité and public instruction through a female allegorical figure.
citation_abnt: ESTAMPES représentant des naïades et Marianne enseignant l'alphabet à des enfants. [1859-1910]. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b10574064v.
notes: Diptych visualizes endurecimento trajectory within single image. LEFT=PRE, RIGHT=POST purification. Atlas: Painel IV.

title: La République aimable (Félicien Rops)
description: Satirical engraving by Belgian-French artist Félicien Rops depicting 'The Amiable Republic' — a subversive or eroticized representation of the Republic as a woman. Critical for understanding the contested gendered nature of republican allegory and its use in satirical press.
citation_abnt: ROPS, Félicien. La République aimable. 1871. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b531842166.
notes: ESSENTIAL counter-example. 1871 Commune/Thiers = zero-point for Third Republic purification. Tag: #contra-alegoria. Atlas: Painel VII.

title: The French Crisis: Madame La République
description: Political cartoon from 1887 showing 'Madame La République' during the French political crisis. The Republic personified as a woman under stress — a key document of how female allegory was deployed during political instability.
citation_abnt: THE FRENCH crisis: Madame La République. 1887. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b8438243t.

title: La République nous appelle... (Steinlen)
description: WWI recruitment poster: 'The Republic calls us...' — Marianne as a summoning female figure, calling citizens to arms. Steinlen's powerful composition shows the Republic-as-woman as a quasi-maternal/military figure demanding sacrifice.
citation_abnt: STEINLEN, Théophile Alexandre. La République nous appelle. 1915. 1 litografia. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/9200518/ark__12148_btv1b10510623s.

title: Buste de la République (Agence Rol)
description: Press photograph of a bust sculpture representing the French Republic. Busts of Marianne became ubiquitous in French town halls (mairies) under the Third Republic — the multiplication of the female allegorical form across thousands of civic spaces.
citation_abnt: BUSTE de la République. [s.d.]. 1 fotografia de imprensa. Agence Rol. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/9200518/ark__12148_btv1b6952880n.

title: Le hochet de la République (Jean Veber)
description: Satirical print 'The Rattle of the Republic' by Jean Veber. The Republic as a woman reduced to a toy or rattle — a critical/ironic commentary on the infantilization or trivialization of republican symbolism through its female form.
citation_abnt: VEBER, Jean. Le hochet de la République. [s.d.]. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://www.europeana.eu/en/item/9200518/ark__12148_btv1b8577646g.

title: Illustrations de Calendrier et compost des bergiers (Danse macabre — female Justice figure)
description: Illustrations from the 'Calendar and Almanac of Shepherds' featuring the dance of death and allegorical figures including Justice. An early representation of Justice as a female figure within the memento mori tradition — the intersection of death, morality, and law.
citation_abnt: CALENDRIER et compost des bergiers: La grant danse macabre. 1531. Manuscrito ilustrado. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/.

title: La Liberté guidant le peuple (Eugène Delacroix)
description: 'Liberty Leading the People' — the iconic image of the July Revolution of 1830. A bare-breasted female figure (Liberty/Marianne) leads armed citizens over barricades, holding the tricolour flag and a musket. The most powerful visual crystallization of the republic-as-woman — Warner's central case study, Agulhon's key image. Foundational for the entire Iconocracy project.
citation_abnt: DELACROIX, Eugène. La Liberté guidant le peuple. 1830. 1 pintura, óleo sobre tela, 260 × 325 cm. Musée du Louvre, Paris. Disponível em: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Eug%C3%A8ne_Delacroix_-_Le_28_Juillet._La_Libert%C3%A9_guidant_le_peuple.jpg.

title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen
description: Engraved broadside of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen (1789), designed by Le Barbier l'aîné and engraved by Laurent and Dien. The composition frames the text of the Declaration with two female allegorical figures — Liberty with Phrygian cap and Justice with scales — flanking a radiating triangle (Eye of Providence). Canonical image of Revolutionary visual rhetoric fusing law, allegory, and print.
citation_abnt: LE BARBIER L'AÎNÉ (des.); LAURENT, L. (grav.); DIEN (grav.). Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen. 1789. 1 estampe. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b69480451.

title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen (variante)
description: Anonymous engraved broadside variant of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen (1789). Presents the text of the Declaration within an allegorical decorative framework featuring female figures. Variant edition circulating alongside the canonical Le Barbier design, reflecting the proliferation of allegorical print culture during the Revolution.
citation_abnt: DÉCLARATION des droits de l'homme et du citoyen (variante). 1789. 1 estampe. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b8410817c.

title: Allégorie pour le frontispice du compte-rendu au Roi par M. Necker
description: Engraved allegorical frontispiece designed for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781), the public financial report that became a landmark in Ancien Régime transparency. Female allegorical figures — variously interpreted as Justice, Abundance, and Truth — frame the royal accounting. An early instance of female allegory deployed in the visual rhetoric of fiscal governance.
citation_abnt: ALLÉGORIE pour le frontispice du compte-rendu au Roi par M. Necker. 1781. 1 estampe. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b8410270p.

title: Allégorie pour le frontispice du compte rendu au Roi par M. Necker (variante)
description: Second variant of the allegorical engraving designed as frontispiece for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781). Female allegorical figures in a variant compositional arrangement. Documents the multiple print versions in circulation around this seminal text on royal finances and public accountability.
citation_abnt: ALLÉGORIE pour le frontispice du compte rendu au Roi par M. Necker (variante). 1781. 1 estampe. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b6942595s.

title: Allégorie pour servir de frontispice au compte-rendu au Roi par M. Necker
description: Third allegorical engraving serving as frontispiece for Necker's 'Compte rendu au Roi' (1781). This variant reinforces the corpus of female allegorical imagery mobilized around the question of royal fiscal accountability in the late Ancien Régime. The three Necker frontispieces (FR-015, FR-016, FR-017) together document the visual politics of the transparency debate.
citation_abnt: ALLÉGORIE pour servir de frontispice au compte-rendu au Roi par M. Necker. 1781. 1 estampe. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b8410268m.

title: [Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité — portrait allégorique d'Ernouf]
description: Revolutionary allegorical print combining the motto Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité with a portrait of Ernouf. Designed by Garneray and engraved by Quéverdo, this composite image exemplifies the visual culture of the Directory period, deploying female allegorical figures to embody Republican values alongside the honored portrait. Documents the consolidation of Marianne iconography in post-Terror Republican print culture.
citation_abnt: GARNERAY (des.); QUÉVERDO (grav.). [Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité — portrait allégorique d'Ernouf]. c. 1793–1800. 1 estampe. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b8412560z.

title: Journée du Poilu, 25 et 26 décembre 1915, organisée par le Parlement
description: WWI charity poster by Steinlen (1915) for the 'Journée du Poilu' (Soldier's Day, December 25–26), organized by the French Parliament to raise funds for soldiers at the front. The composition depicts a French soldier in the foreground, with a female figure — embodying the Republic/Marianne — in an embrace or gesture of support behind him. One of Steinlen's key contributions to French WWI visual culture, combining social realism with Republican allegorical tradition.
citation_abnt: STEINLEN, Théophile Alexandre. Journée du Poilu, 25 et 26 décembre 1915, organisée par le Parlement. 1915. 1 affiche (litografia). Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b9012753r.

title: Decretum Gratiani (manuscrito iluminado, BnF)
description: Manuscrito iluminado do Decretum Gratiani (Concordia discordantium canonum, c. 1140), coletânea de direito canônico compilada pelo monge Graciano em Bolonha, conservado na Bibliothèque nationale de France. Os manuscritos do Decretum são célebres por suas miniaturas iluminadas — especialmente capitais historiadas e frontispícios — que representam a Justitia como figura feminina com espada e balança, cenas de julgamento e disputas jurídicas. Produzido nos scriptoria bolonheses no século XIII, o exemplar da BnF integra a tradição dos manuscritos jurídicos iluminados que constituem o principal corpus medieval da iconografia da justiça. Digitalizado e disponível na plataforma Gallica.
citation_abnt: GRACIANO. Decretum Gratiani (Concordia discordantium canonum). [Bolonha], séc. XIII. 1 manuscrito iluminado, pergaminho. Paris: Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b10544534k.item. Acesso em: 28 mar. 2026.

title: La Liberté guidant le peuple
description: Pintura icônica de Delacroix representando a Liberdade como mulher com barrete frígio, seio nu, empunhando a bandeira tricolor e um mosquete, guiando o povo sobre barricadas durante a Revolução de Julho de 1830. Figura central da iconografia republicana francesa.
citation_abnt: La Liberté guidant le peuple

title: Notre-Dame des colonies
description: Litografia satírica de Jean Veber representando uma Marianne como "Nossa Senhora das Colônias" — paródia da iconografia religiosa e republicana a serviço da crítica ao imperialismo colonial francês. A figura feminina é apresentada com atributos marianos e coloniais simultaneamente.
citation_abnt: Notre-Dame des colonies

title: Bons de la Défense nationale
description: Cartaz de propaganda para bônus de defesa nacional durante a Primeira Guerra Mundial. Marianne aparece como figura convocatória, associada a símbolos patrióticos e militares, incentivando a subscrição de empréstimos de guerra.
citation_abnt: Bons de la Défense nationale

title: Emprunt national 1920 (Société générale)
description: Cartaz do Empréstimo Nacional de 1920, patrocinado pela Société Générale. Marianne aparece como símbolo de reconstrução nacional no imediato pós-guerra, associada à estabilidade financeira e à continuidade republicana.
citation_abnt: Emprunt national 1920 (Société générale)

title: Emprunt national 1920 (Banque Nationale de Paris et des Pays-Bas)
description: Cartaz do Empréstimo Nacional de 1920, patrocinado pela Banque Nationale de Paris et des Pays-Bas. Variante institucional-bancária do cartaz de empréstimo, com Marianne em registro solene e institucional.
citation_abnt: Emprunt national 1920 (Banque Nationale de Paris et des Pays-Bas)

title: Emprunt de la Libération (Rente française 1918)
description: Cartaz do Empréstimo da Libertação (1918), marcando a transição guerra–paz. Marianne/Liberté é invocada simultaneamente como símbolo de vitória militar e de reconstrução, em registro entre o MILITAR e o NORMATIVO.
citation_abnt: Emprunt de la Libération (Rente française 1918)

title: Prêtez à la France pour qu'elle grandisse dans le rayonnement de la Paix!
description: Cartaz do Comptoir National d'Escompte de Paris (1920). "Empreste à França para que ela cresça no esplendor da Paz!" — Marianne é associada à Paz e ao crescimento nacional, num registro pós-bélico de transição para a normalidade institucional.
citation_abnt: Prêtez à la France pour qu'elle grandisse dans le rayonnement de la Paix!

title: Emprunt national 1920 (Société centrale des banques de province)
description: Cartaz do Empréstimo Nacional de 1920, emitido pela Société centrale des banques de province. Distribuição provincial do programa de empréstimos nacionais, com Marianne como signo de unidade nacional.
citation_abnt: Emprunt national 1920 (Société centrale des banques de province)

title: En avant! Armée de l'Épargne, c'est pour la Patrie
description: Cartaz de propaganda "Em frente! Exército da Poupança, é pela Pátria" (1916). Linguagem militarizada aplicada à economia de guerra — a poupança é apresentada como forma de serviço militar, com Marianne como comandante simbólica do "exército" dos poupadores.
citation_abnt: En avant! Armée de l'Épargne, c'est pour la Patrie

title: Madame Anastasie (avec les ciseaux de la censure)
description: Capa de L'Éclipse no. 209: velha quase surda e cega agarrando tesouras enormes — personificação da censura da imprensa. Encarna o aparato repressivo do governo da Ordem Moral sob MacMahon. A "Anastasie" de Gill tornou-se a representação icônica francesa da censura.
citation_abnt: Madame Anastasie (avec les ciseaux de la censure)

title: La Paix — Idylle
description: Litografia da série Actualités: paisagem devastada de ruínas após a Guerra Franco-Prussiana. O título irônico "Paz — Idílio" transforma o gênero pastoral/feminino do idílio em cena de destruição total.
citation_abnt: La Paix — Idylle

title: L'Empire c'est la paix
description: Litografia da série Actualités: campo de ruínas e ossos com inscrição sarcástica citando o motto inaugural de Napoleão III. A figura feminina alegórica da França/Paz está conspicuamente ausente da paisagem devastada.
citation_abnt: L'Empire c'est la paix

title: Calendrier républicain (An III)
description: Republican calendar (Year III) in two engraved panels. Upper register features female allegorical figures flanking a central medallion with fasces and Phrygian cap. Left panel: Liberty and Equality with civic attributes; right panel: agricultural scene under arched pediment. Columns of calendar months below in republican nomenclature. Decorative border with diamond patterns and medallions.
citation_abnt: QUÉVÉDO, François-Marie-Isidore. Calendrier républicain (An III). 1794. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: Gallica.
notes: Interesting liminal object — between foundational propaganda and normative bureaucratic instrument. Low endurecimento consistent with revolutionary dynamism. Small-scale figures limit detailed indicator coding.

title: Liberté (d'après Moitte)
description: Seated female Liberty holding a Phrygian cap aloft on a pole in her right hand. Classical drapery, laurel crown. Seated on a stone pedestal inscribed 'LIBERTÉ'. Left arm rests on fasces bound with ribbons. Serpent crushed beneath the pedestal. Dark background emphasizing the sculptural white figure. After a design by sculptor Moitte.
citation_abnt: MOITTE, Jean-Guillaume. Liberté. 1792. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: Gallica.
notes: Strong sculptural presence. Desincorporação=2 because of heavy classicizing that removes corporeal individuality. Fasces + inscription = heraldization. Transitional toward normativo but still foundational energy in the raised arm.

title: La Liberté, soutenue par la Raison, protège l'Innocence et couronne la Vertu
description: Multi-figure allegorical composition. Winged Liberty at left crowns Virtue (seated right, holding radiant mirror/sun). Reason at center steadies the scene. Innocence crouches at Virtue's feet. Lion at far right. Five female figures in classical drapery arranged in a sculptural relief composition. Inscription below: 'La Liberté, soutenue par la Raison, protège l'Innocence et couronne la Vertu'. After a design by Boizot.
citation_abnt: BOIZOT, Louis-Simon. La Liberté, soutenue par la Raison, protège l'Innocence et couronne la Vertu. 1793. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: Gallica.
notes: Very low endurecimento — narrative is rich (apagamento_narrativo=0), bodies are dynamic and differentiated. Quintessentially foundational: Liberty still has wings, still acts. Compare with FR-040 (companion piece) for same series.

title: Iustitia (d'après Bruegel)
description: Panoramic allegorical engraving of Justice (Iustitia) from Bruegel's Seven Virtues series. Central female figure of Justice stands blindfolded with sword and scales, surrounded by scenes of juridical punishment: scaffolds, flogging, public execution, interrogation, courtroom proceedings. Latin inscription: 'SCOPVS LEGIS EST AVT VT EVQVE PVNIT EMENDET, AVT POENA EIVS CAETEROS MELIORES REDDAT AVT SVBLATIS MALIS CAETERI SECVRIORES VIVANT'.
citation_abnt: BRUEGEL, Pieter, o Velho; GALLE, Philips. Iustitia. 1559. 1 gravura. Série: As Sete Virtudes. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: Gallica.
notes: Out of temporal scope (1559) but essential genealogical reference. Very low endurecimento — rich narrative, embodied figure, no bureaucratic hardening. Pre-foundational: the tradition from which 19th-c. allegory descends.

title: [Virtudes cardinales: Justica] (La Patria Ilustrada)
description: Litografia de José Guadalupe Posada publicada na revista mexicana La Patria Ilustrada (Cidade do México, 18 fev. 1889), integrante da série 'Virtudes cardinales' (Virtudes cardinais). A imagem representa a Justiça (Justica/Justitia) como figura feminina alegórica, retomando a iconografia greco-romana da Iustitia em contexto da imprensa ilustrada porfirista. Posada, o mais importante gravador popular mexicano, trabalhou para diversas publicações periódicas e produziu um vocabulário iconográfico de grande alcance para o imaginário político e moral mexicano. O exemplar é conservado na Yale University, Sterling Memorial Library, Latin American Collection, e digitalizado pela Library of Congress.
citation_abnt: POSADA, José Guadalupe. [Virtudes cardinales: Justica]. La Patria Ilustrada, Cidade do México, 18 fev. 1889. 1 litografia, 23,5 × 16 cm. Washington: Library of Congress. Disponível em: https://www.loc.gov/item/2003656173/. Acesso em: 28 mar. 2026.

title: Vrouwe Justitia (nude, with sword and scales)
description: 16th-century engraving of Vrouwe Justitia — nude, holding sword in right hand, scales at left, appearing to trample a child underfoot. A muscular, powerful rendering of female Justice — far from the idealized classical model.
citation_abnt: VROUWE Justitia (nua, com espada e balança). 1500–1600. 1 gravura. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/object/Vrouwe-Justitia--13997b5b276f9bbbb36a847da4c3022a.

title: Justitia (bust with crown and eye pendant)
description: Bust of a woman with a crown and a necklace bearing an eye pendant, identified in inscription as Justitia. The all-seeing eye as a Justice attribute — surveillance and omniscience as female qualities of law.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA (busto com coroa e olho pendente). [s.d.]. 1 escultura (busto). Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/object/Justitia--314f580f935ba978fb199ce7abeb0db1.

title: Allegorie op de rechtvaardigheid (Allegory of Justice, enthroned)
description: Title page with enthroned Justice (Rechtvaardigheid) on a pedestal. At her feet, attributes symbolizing worldly power. The throne-composition as a visual argument for the sovereignty of law over political authority.
citation_abnt: ALLEGORIE op de rechtvaardigheid. Século XVII. 1 gravura (página de título). Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/object/Allegorie-op-de-rechtvaardigheid--a26144337b14ab57eb5ca23025308032.

title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
description: Engraving depicting Justice (Justitia) as a female allegorical figure, attributed to Jacob Matham after a design by Hendrick Goltzius. Part of a series on the virtues. Justitia shown standing, holding a sword and scales, blindfolded.
citation_abnt: MATHAM, Jacob (attr.). Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia). 1585–1589. 1 gravura. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-OB-27.296.

title: Vrouwe Justitia voor het oordeel van Zaleucus en het oordeel van Cambyses
description: Engraving by Willem Jacobsz Delff depicting Lady Justice (Vrouwe Justitia) presiding over the Judgment of Zaleucus and the Judgment of Cambyses — two classical exempla of justice. Female allegorical figure with sword and scales flanked by historical judicial scenes.
citation_abnt: DELFF, Willem Jacobsz. Vrouwe Justitia voor het oordeel van Zaleucus en het oordeel van Cambyses. 1590–1638. 1 gravura. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-1883-A-6992.

title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
description: Engraving of Justice (Justitia) as a female allegorical figure, made by Jacob Matham after Hendrick Goltzius in 1597. Part of the series depicting the Four Cardinal Virtues. Justitia stands with sword and scales.
citation_abnt: MATHAM, Jacob. Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia). 1597. 1 gravura. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-OB-27.124.

title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia) / Iustitia
description: Anonymous engraving of Justice (Iustitia) after the design tradition of Hendrick Goltzius and Jacob Matham. Female allegorical figure representing Justitia with the traditional attributes of sword and scales. Undated impression from the period 1585–1637.
citation_abnt: ANONIEM. Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia) / Iustitia. 1585–1637. 1 gravura. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-1882-A-6499.

title: Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia)
description: Engraving of Justice (Rechtvaardigheid / Justitia) by Jacob Matham, 1593. Female allegorical figure in classical dress, holding the sword and scales — canonical attributes of Justitia in Northern European legal iconography of the late 16th century.
citation_abnt: MATHAM, Jacob. Rechtvaardigheid (Justitia). 1593. 1 gravura. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Disponível em: https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-1887-A-12280.

title: Justiça popular (UDP political poster)
description: Political poster from the Portuguese revolutionary period (post-Carnation Revolution, 1974): 'Popular Justice: the PIDE agent who murdered Dias Coelho will be judged at the people's cost!' Justice invoked in revolutionary political context — a moment when the concept of Justice was being radically renegotiated.
citation_abnt: UNIÃO DEMOCRÁTICA POPULAR. Justiça popular: o Pide que assassinou Dias Coelho vai ser julgado nas costas do povo! [1975?]. 1 cartaz. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/17148-justica-popular.

title: Alegoria à História (female allegorical engraving)
description: Historical allegorical engraving featuring female figures representing History. An early modern Portuguese example of the female allegorical tradition — History personified as a woman, part of the same visual vocabulary that produced Justice and Republic figures.
citation_abnt: [ALEGORIA à História]. c. 1600. 1 gravura, água-forte, p&b. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/39213-alegoria-a-historia.

title: Alegoria à Morte (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
description: Allegorical engraving representing Death, part of a series of allegorical works by the French-Portuguese artist Quillard produced in Lisbon. Demonstrates the French-Portuguese artistic exchange in allegorical visual culture during the Baroque period.
citation_abnt: QUILLARD, Pierre Antoine. Alegoria à Morte. 1730. 1 gravura. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/37491-alegoria-a-morte.

title: Alegoria ao Tempo (Pierre Antoine Quillard)
description: Allegorical engraving representing Time, companion piece to the Alegoria à Morte. Part of Quillard's allegorical series produced in Lisbon. Time as a personified figure — part of the broader iconographic programme where abstract concepts (Justice, Time, Truth, Death) take human form.
citation_abnt: QUILLARD, Pierre Antoine. Alegoria ao Tempo. 1730. 1 gravura. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/records/item/37507-alegoria-ao-tempo.

title: A Republica precisa de ti: vota em Norton de Matos
description: Electoral poster from the 1949 Portuguese presidential campaign featuring a female allegorical figure representing the Portuguese Republic. 'The Republic needs you: vote for Norton de Matos.' A classical female figure in robes symbolizes the Republic during a period of authoritarian governance — the allegory deployed as opposition to dictatorship.
citation_abnt: A REPUBLICA precisa de ti: vota em Norton de Matos. 1949. 1 cartaz. Comissão Distrital do Porto. Biblioteca Nacional de Portugal. Disponível em: https://bndigital.bnportugal.gov.pt/.

title: 1 Escudo "Alvorada" — Primeira República Portuguesa
description: Figura feminina da República com barrete frígio, agitando tocha acesa, bandeira portuguesa no braço e sol nascente ao fundo. Inscrição: 5 DE OUTUBRO DE 1910. A "Alvorada" é a Marianne portuguesa: importação explícita da gramática visual republicana francesa adaptada à mitologia fundacional lusófona.

title: Série Ceres — Selo definitivo da República Portuguesa
description: Primeira série definitiva de selos após a proclamação da República, substituindo selos com retrato de D. Manuel II. Deusa romana Ceres de pé, segurando foice e feixe de trigo. A escolha de Ceres (abundância agrícola) sobre figura marcial reflete a narrativa republicana de soberania popular enraizada no trabalho.
citation_abnt: Série Ceres — Selo definitivo da República Portuguesa

title: La Liberté armée du Sceptre de la Raison foudroye l'Ignorance et le Fanatisme
description: Companion piece to FR-039. Liberty seated at center, flanked by standing Reason at left (with lion). Reason wields a radiant scepter/sun-disk emitting lightning bolts that strike Ignorance and Fanaticism (male/ambiguous figures recoiling at right). Liberty holds Reason's arm. Dark background, bas-relief composition. Inscription: 'La Liberté armée du Sceptre de la Raison foudroye l'Ignorance et le Fanatisme'.
citation_abnt: BOIZOT, Louis-Simon. La Liberté armée du Sceptre de la Raison foudroye l'Ignorance et le Fanatisme. 1793. 1 gravura. Bibliothèque nationale de France. Disponível em: Gallica.
notes: Slightly higher endurecimento than FR-039 — Liberty is more static (seated), heraldization begins (lion as attribute). But narrative richness (apagamento=0) and dynamic combat scene keep it foundational. Paired with FR-039 in Boizot's series.

title: 25 Mark — Stadtsparkasse Bielefeld (Notgeld), Bielefelder Jungbronnen (Fountain of Youth), silk note
description: Weimar-era silk emergency currency (Notgeld) issued by Stadtsparkasse Bielefeld in 1921, celebrating the city's 700th anniversary. The obverse features a "Jungbrunnen" (fountain of youth) allegory: crippled figures enter a healing pool and emerge healed, with references to maidens keeping watch and medical attestations. The reverse offers a satirical commentary on local textile dye works polluting the Lutterbach river.

title: Crispim do Amaral, Alegoria da República (pano de boca do Theatro da Paz, Belém, 1890), reproduzida em Lima Junior (2020)
description: Seated female allegory of the Brazilian Republic enthroned. Wears white classical dress with green mantle (national colors), laurel crown with red Phrygian cap, golden necklace. Right hand rests on a sword, left hand on the throne's armrest with lion-head finials. Palm frond at her feet. Background mosaic inscription 'ESTADOS UNIDOS DO BRASIL' with Roman numeral MDCCCLXXXIX (1889, date of Republic proclamation). Ornamental border with blue rosettes.
citation_abnt: LIMA JUNIOR, Carlos Rogério. Marianne à brasileira: imagens republicanas e os dilemas do Brasil nos finais do século XIX. 2020. Tese (Doutorado em História) — Faculdade de Filosofia, Letras e Ciências Humanas, Universidade de São Paulo, São Paulo, 2020. Reprodução: Alegoria da República (pano de boca do Theatro da Paz, Belém, 1890), de Crispim do Amaral.
notes: Key foundational painting for BR corpus. Endurecimento moderate — heraldization and architectural framing are strong (throne, mosaic), but body retains some dynamism through the green mantle draping. Sword is decorative, not raised.

title: Lady Justice (F.W. Pomeroy, Old Bailey, London)
description: The iconic gold statue of Lady Justice atop the Old Bailey, London's Central Criminal Court. Notably unblindfolded — holding sword and scales, with spiked crown. The courthouse brochures explain that 'her maidenly form is supposed to guarantee her impartiality.' A prime example of how the female body itself is argued to embody legal virtue.
citation_abnt: POMEROY, Frederick William. Lady Justice. 1907. 1 escultura em bronze dourado. Central Criminal Court (Old Bailey), London. Disponível em: http://www.speel.me.uk/sculptlondon/oldbaileyjustice.htm.

title: Woman holding sword and scales of justice (Jurisprudentia)
description: Engraving by Étienne Delaune (c. 1560) depicting a female figure holding a sword and scales — the canonical attributes of Justice — identified as Jurisprudentia. Delaune was a French goldsmith and engraver active in mid-16th century France and Germany; this work, held at the Wellcome Collection, exemplifies Renaissance allegorical personification of law and jurisprudence.
citation_abnt: DELAUNE, Étienne. Woman holding sword and scales of justice (Jurisprudentia). c. 1560. 1 gravura. Wellcome Collection, London. Disponível em: https://wellcomecollection.org/works/rkvhanzr.
notes: Confirmed 1.0. UK baseline. Note: 'UK' by collection (Wellcome), not origin (French artist).

title: Women of Britain Say 'Go!'
description: British WWI recruitment poster by E.J. Kealey (1915), published by the Parliamentary Recruiting Committee (Poster No. 75). Shows two women and a boy at an open window watching soldiers march away. The female figures embody a gendered allegory of domestic Britain urging men to enlist — deploying the moral authority of womanhood as surrogate for national female personification. One of the most iconic British WWI images, widely reproduced and analysed in the history of gender and war propaganda.
citation_abnt: KEALEY, Ernest James. Women of Britain say 'Go!'. 1915. 1 litografia colorida (cartaz). Imperial War Museum, London. Disponível em: https://www.iwm.org.uk/collections/item/object/14592.
notes: Confirmed 1.7. Borderline case: heraldizacao=2 debatable — bodies themselves become heraldic signs. Needs methodological note in thesis.

notes: AI first-pass (iconocode-sonnet5), imagem única digitalizada via portinari.org.br, sem inspecao fisica. Cena narrativa (Juizo de Salomao) com duas figuras femininas (mae desfalecida/aflita + testemunha) em composicao cubista/grisalha -- nao e personificacao pura, mas engaja diretamente iconografia de julgamento (Iustitia). inscricao_estatal=1 e estimativa (Portinari pintou multiplas obras para predios federais, mas nao confirmei comitente/instalacao desta obra especifica). Tensao estilistica com contra-alegoria (fragmentacao cubista contesta o cânone classico) nao capturada pelo campo regime_iconocratico (script so aceita fundacional/normativo/militar) -- avaliar se contra-alegoria e mais apropriado. Pendente auditoria de Ana.
